content.figure: Figure 6: The 0 h/1 h or 0 h/2 h rule-out and rule-in algorithms using high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) assays in patients presenting to the emergency department with suspected NSTEMI and without an indication for immediate invasive angiography.

classification_pathways.rule-out_pathway: Patients with a very low initial hs-cTn value OR a low initial hs-cTn value with no rise at 1 h/2 h are assigned to the rule-out pathway.
classification_pathways.observe_pathway: Patients who do not meet the criteria for either rule-out or rule-in are assigned to the observe pathway; these patients should have hs-cTn levels checked at 3 h and echocardiography to decide further management.
classification_pathways.rule-in_pathway: Patients with a high initial hs-cTn value OR an increase at 1 h/2 h in hs-cTn are assigned to the rule-in pathway.

definitions_and_notes.cutoffs: Cut-offs are assay specific (see Supplementary material online, Table S4) and derived to meet pre-defined criteria for sensitivity and specificity for NSTEMI.
definitions_and_notes.management_decision: Appropriate management can be determined based on the hs-cTn levels and the clinical situation.
definitions_and_notes.footnote: Rule-out pathway applicability note: only applicable if chest pain onset was >3 h prior to the 0 h hs-cTn measurement (per figure footnote).

clinical_actions: Rule-out pathway => consider discharge or noninvasive management per clinical context.
Observe pathway => repeat hs-cTn at 3 h and perform echocardiography to guide further management.
Rule-in pathway => consider diagnosis of NSTEMI and proceed with appropriate invasive or medical management as indicated.
references_mentioned: Main text sections for potential management and testing options
